core_obligations: Build the compact-support/topological devissage for the needed torus n-torsion multiplicative-type complexes and their finite-etale Cartier duals, including the nonsmooth characteristic-prime torsion cases. Do not assume the displayed proof works for arbitrary finite-flat kernels.
Establish ell-primary duality through finite/profinite Kummer diagrams, controlling divisible kernels by Tate modules and excluding invalid direct-limit steps at ell=p.
Prove finite D-group pairings and stabilization to Sha on proper opens U!=X, strictness of global images and exactness under the specifically justified inverse/direct limits.
Assemble the global long sequence and identify exactly the two places requiring completed local products; do not assume the sought Poitou–Tate theorem.

proof_roadmap.step: Mapping-cone compact support and strict topologies, finite-complex devissage and profiniteness.
Torus cohomology finiteness/vanishing; finite-flat complex duality; ell-primary Kummer limits with divisible kernel control.
Pass from finite diagrams to perfect torsion/completion pairings, then local-global D-pairings.
Stabilize finite kernels on sufficiently small opens, identify Sha, prove discrete global image and ptstart exactness.
Take direct limits for ordinary rows; use strict Pontryagin duality, unramified annihilators and Sha duality for the three linking sequences.

difficulty_reason: The complete torus-complex solution must construct compatible compact-support topologies, control finite and possibly infinite characteristic-p Kummer systems, remove divisible kernels through Tate modules, stabilize finiteD-groups on proper opens, and justify strict limit and Pontryagin-dual exactness for the restricted-product groups. Both independent reviewers support H3 for these interacting arithmetic/topological obligations, with the visible finite-flat application scope and source-display readings. No global Poitou–Tate theorem is supplied as input and the final diagram alone is not the basis of the grade.

source_issues.decision: Over U=Spec(F_p[t]), multiplication by t on alpha_p gives a map between finite-flat group schemes whose kernel has coordinate algebra F_p[t,x]/(x^p,t*x), not flat over F_p[t]. Thus taking A=ker(f_r) in the general finite-flat devissage does not automatically keep the induction inside finite-flat groups. In this task the complexes actually used in1349 are built from n-torsion of tori (finite multiplicative type) and their Cartier-dual finite etale groups. These subcategories are etale-locally finite modules under Cartier duality, so their kernels and quotients remain finite flat, and the author induction applies to the needed cases. State this application boundary visibly; do not invent a proof for arbitrary finite-flat complexes.

source_issues.explanation: The defining hat C=[hat T2->hat T1] and devis2 at549-555 are consistent and correct. Contrary to the initial selector concern, devis2 itself is not reversed. The five-lemma diagram882-886 reverses the torus labels and prints an unjustified initial0. Use the cohomology segment already printed in devis2, without asserting injectivity of its first arrow. The isomorphisms in degrees0,1 and injection in degree2 are independently established in855-877, so the intended five-lemma implication is fixed without adding a new argument.

The quotient used to topologize Hc^i is the local degree(i-1) quotient in the printed sequence405, whereas435 prints degree i. At431 the right group should carry the generic degree i of427-428. More substantially,451 cannot generally call the outer group finite/discrete: Hc^2(U,mu_p) may be infinite, as the same author explicitly notes at1578. The already specified strict devissage expresses the middle group as an extension of closed-subgroup/quotient profinite terms by induction; a strict Hausdorff extension of profinite groups is profinite. Indeed quotient by a compact kernel is a closed map with compact fibers, so compactness lifts from the quotient, and connected components map trivially into the totally disconnected quotient and then lie trivially in the kernel. This uses the author devissage unchanged and only the weaker profinite premise that its own induction provides. Do not reproduce the stronger finite assertion as a proved fact.

The finite D-pairings must be read with U!=X. Their proofs explicitly invoke finite-group lemmas849,2003,2031 having that hypothesis, and the counted main proof chooses U!=X at2539-2540. The unrestricted auxiliary wording cannot be endorsed: for C=Gm and U=X, D1=Pic(X) has its nonzero degree subgroup and is not finite. All shrinking/stabilization arguments may and in the main proof do start with a proper open. This is an explicit scope restriction to the already used branch, not a repair of the counted global theorem.

C_(r+11) at1280 is the adjacent C_(r+1) already defined in350 and1306. In finidiag2, the lower central term1693-1694 must be H^(1+i)(U,C tensor Z/ell^m)^*: its neighboring Kummer terms are (ell^m H^(2+i)(U,C))^* and (H^(1+i)(U,C)/ell^m)^*, and avfini pairs the upper degree -i with1+i. At1815 the second repeated hat T2 must be hat T1, as fixed by devis2 and the lower T2/T1 dual row. These are uniquely determined labels; do not alter the stored author equations.

The finite H1(U,T2) invoked at908 is fini1(a), not the character-lattice h1lem(a). The central isomorphism at1916 is avfini2 as already identified at1718 and1934. In2042 the object injecting into D2(U,hat M) is D2(U,hat C), by the printed devistmbis triangle and vanishing H3(U,hat T); the text instead prints hat T. The initial0 in2307-2308 is not part of the full cohomology exact sequence: the preceding H0(M) may have nonzero image in H0(F), and the argument only needs the displayed segment from H0(F) onward, with its first vertical map an isomorphism. The generic-i argument2386 uses H^i, not only H1. Finally2549 must cite refin1(a), the actual pairing printed1857-1866, not refin2. Each required mathematical statement is already present in the selected author text.

At2360 the unramified subgroup in degree i is the image of H^i(O_v,C) in the completed H^i(K_v,C), not the fixed H1 printed there. This is forced by the definition of Hnr in the retained setup and by the actual degrees -1 and0 in2531/2534 and2603-2610.
